title: Recycle handoff (post-order) at the WCLI-50 / WCLI-52 boundary
description:
Written to order by the orchestrator's recycle notice of 2026-09-29 ~14:30Z, which asked for a handoff written AFTER the request rather than only the one WCLI-55 already carried. WCLI-55 has the full account of the session; this record states the boundary as it stands now, what moved since WCLI-55, and the successor's next work. Every ref below was read back from the remote.

STATE AT HANDOVER, read from the refs. origin/main == origin/dev == fac0152. 0 open PRs. Tree clean, branch dev. Tracker: WCLI-50 Done (delivered in opum-ai/ward-cli#103, squash baf6e0f, promoted), WCLI-55 Done (the first handoff record, #105), WCLI-52 / WCLI-53 / WCLI-14 To Do, NOTHING In Progress (quest task list --status "In Progress" with scope.otherRefsRead true and unseenTaskIds empty before the last two commits). The cursor was written by this session's bound flush, opum-workflow 0.11.0.

WHAT MOVED SINCE WCLI-55. Two tracker-only commits and their promotions: #107 (fac0152) adds an additive correction note to WCLI-50's completed record - the reviewer's closure pass caught that the amended AC4's closing clause claimed the base model also produces the behaviour, which the gate's without-arm contradicts (it scores below the with-arm on every adversarial case, and leaked the literal value in all three history runs); the criterion is left as written history and the note carries the correction. #106 and #108 kept main level with dev. Nothing behaviour-relevant changed after the reviewed bytes: the reviewer verified blob-for-blob that what it reviewed (c435b15) is what shipped.

WHAT THE SESSION DELIVERED, summarised so the successor does not have to reconstruct it: the ward skill hardened at skills/ward/SKILL.md with one rule per surface the operator named (session transcript, stdout/stderr, shell history, redaction of an already-emitted value); the opum-ward plugin skeleton (the minimum of WCLI-14's packaging the gate needed - extend it, do not re-create); evals/ with five cases (four adversarial, one should-NOT-fire guard); scripts/check-evals.mjs vendored from opum-fleet with provenance and wired into CI as eval:check; scripts/run-eval.sh as the billed release gate, deliberately not in any workflow; spec 11.3 corrected for the private-phase distribution; CLAUDE.md's skill pointer updated. The recorded gate on the merged bytes: 5/5 at threshold, score 1.000, mean delta 0.500, 0 errored runs, per-case deltas 0.50/0.50/1.00/0.50 for the adversarial cases and 0.00 for the guard.

SUCCESSOR NEXT WORK, in order, and do not start ahead of the renewal kickoff: WCLI-52 (the backup/restore residual the WCLI-51 review found untracked), then WCLI-53 (the CI flake: key-provider.test.ts:293 plus the three extra wall-clock ceilings added to it on the OPAG-768 relay - backup.test.ts:538, setup.test.ts:201, vault-store.test.ts:626 - and a sweep of the rest of the suite).

NOT TO RE-DERIVE, each paid for here and also on WCLI-55: the full gate costs about 29 minutes and $9.77 list-price estimate per run and is a release gate, not a per-edit loop; the isolation procedure is per-case because a whole-suite --ablation none run fails by construction on the guard; a case whose skill does not fire is a defect in the case (the redact prompt was extended for exactly that); any behaviour-relevant edit to the skill or the case files invalidates the recorded gate and the affected pairs; the leak floors grade the final message only, and the tool has no assistant-messages-only target.

OPEN OBLIGATION: OFLE-162's distribution half is opum-fleet's successor's, not this repository's. The entry name (opum-ward), the ref (baf6e0f, on dev and main) and the gate facts were sent to opum-fleet and acknowledged in a cross-session reply; nothing further is owed unless the manifest needs a different ref, in which case the current tips (fac0152) carry everything baf6e0f did.
finalSummary: The post-order handoff the orchestrator's recycle notice asked for: written after the request, so the successor's cursor and this record both postdate it. It states the boundary refs read back from the remote (origin/main == origin/dev == fac0152, 0 open PRs, nothing In Progress), what moved since WCLI-55 (#107's AC4 correction note and its promotions), the session's deliverables in summary, the successor's queue (WCLI-52 then WCLI-53) and the do-not-re-derive list. The cursor was written by this session's bound flush (opum-workflow 0.11.0) after this record was filed, and it is machine-local and gitignored, so this record is the durable half. Closed by the same pull request that lands it.
